messages:
maria: infra-bot alerted on gpu-cc-12: repeated NVIDIA Xid errors (code 13) across GPU0/1, node auto-rebooted twice in 30m. Kicking off triage.

infra-bot: [ALERT] node=gpu-cc-12, gpu=0, xid=13, count=27, metric=nvidia_gpu_xid_errors_total, timestamp=2024-06-23T14:47:10Z

devon: ugh. do we know what jobs were on that node? any correlation to overnight batch runs?

maria: running `kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-cc-12` shows several large training jobs (trainer-mv2-*) and a couple of inference replicas pinned. main spike at 14:20 when a nightly hyperparam sweep started.

maria: pasted snippets — nvidia-smi + dmesg: ```
# nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,CEC
GPU 0:
  FB Memory Usage
    Total                       : 32768 MiB
    Used                        : 29012 MiB
    Free                        : 3756 MiB
  ECC Errors
    Volatile
      Single-bit                : 512
      Double-bit                : 3
dmesg | tail -n 20
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (13) at 0x7fabcde
[ 12345.679012] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 12346.000000] i2c i2c-3: NACK
```

sachin: thanks. initial read: Xid 13 in our infra has historically correlated with memory/ ECC incidents + aggressive mem alloc patterns (huge batch sizes + many concurrent allocations). Not always true but it's the pattern we've seen.

julia: can we verify whether these were single-bit ECC corrections turning into UEs? the `nvidia-smi -q` snippet shows double-bit = 3 which is worrying. if UEs hit, GPU can be marked bad and driver resets occur.

maria: i looked at prometheus: `sum by(code)(increase(nvidia_gpu_xid_errors_total[5m]))` shows code=13 spikes on that node starting 14:19. same timeframe as `trainer-mv2-` pods.

devon: action plan? do we drain/replace the card or try a soft mitigation first?

sachin: recommended triage steps (short):
- cordon & drain node: `kubectl cordon gpu-cc-12` + `kubectl drain gpu-cc-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` (avoid killing checkpointing jobs if possible)
- tag node in inventory with `gpu_xid_13=observed` and update asset owner.
- collect full diagnostics: `sudo journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced --since "1 hour ago"`, `dmesg -T | grep -i Xid`, `/var/log/messages` and attach to ticket.
- run `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=temperature.gpu,clocks.gr ,pstate,power.draw --format=csv -l 1` under controlled load to reproduce.
- if double-bit ECC > 0, schedule replacement — treat as hardware fault.

maria: i've already cordoned and started draining. moving low-priority jobs first. putting node in `maintenance` pool.

julia: for monitoring/alerts we should:
- add alert: `ALERT GPUs_Xid_By_Code` if `increase(nvidia_gpu_xid_errors_total{code!=""}[10m]) > 0` by node for 5m. label with `code` and `gpu_index` so we know which code spikes.
- create derived metric `nvidia_gpu_ecc_uncorrectable_total` and alert on >0 for 1h.
- tag jobs by `workload_type` (train/eval/serving) in our exporter so we can correlate Xid occurrences to workload.

sachin: also keep an eye on power/thermal telemetry — some Xid variants (we see 79 sometimes) co-occur with thermal throttling or PCIe link errors. correlate `node_exporter` metrics: `node_power` and `temp` with Xid events.

devon: regarding replacements — how many spare cards in AZ-1? cost note: pulling a node out for replacement reduces cluster capacity ~4 GPUs; with two nodes down we'd hit 12% capacity loss in training tier today. downtime costs > we should prefer hot-swap vs full replacement where possible.

maria: opened INFRA-7212 with logs + `nvidia-smi -q` dump, set severity=high. assigned to @sachin for HW validation. ticket includes node serial and region.

julia: small ops improvement: add `xid_code` tag to pod telemetry at runtime (we can annotate pods when exporter sees xid from that GPU) — helps aggregate by model.

sachin: long-term detection idea: anomaly detection on per-pod allocation patterns. flag pods that allocate > 75% GPU memory for > 30s and schedule rolling restarts or smaller batch shards. that seems to reduce Xid 13 spikes in our tests.

maria: update: after drain node rebooted and we ran stress test under controlled conditions, GPU0 produced another Xid 13 under sustained mem pressure. double-bit ECC count increased. ordering replacement with vendor.

devon: thanks team. please post postmortem after replacement. for now i'm tagging affected training jobs to avoid rescheduling on same rack. :white_check_mark: 

infra-bot: [INFO] ticket INFRA-7212 created by maria, current_state=investigating, assigned=sachin"
